answer: A bonded staking protocol resists Sybil attacks by requiring agents to lock tokens in an on-chain escrow. This stake acts as an economic anchor for each identity, with protocol validators monitoring each communication thread to slash collateral upon detected fraud. An attacker incurs the verifiable cost of locking scarce financial capital per identity, making hollow mass registrations prohibitive. However, this mechanism restricts capital efficiency and disadvantages underfunded agents.
